text:
Accuracy check on A: it states 84 staff with over eight weeks and $3.9M liability, which is correct. The cap is described correctly (a plan, then a direction of up to a quarter with eight weeks' notice). Cash-out is correct, though it omits that cashing out was previously not allowed (a minor omission). The shutdown is correct. The exemption for 24/7 warehouse staff is correct, including that they are still covered by the cap and cash-out. It omits the leave-without-pay and make-up-time options. The action is correct: lists go to managers by 31 October. A is word-efficient, at around 120 words or just under.

Accuracy check on B: "Staff with over eight weeks are asked to agree a reduction plan" softens "will need to," which is mildly misleading. "Eight weeks' notice given" is fine. The cash-out mentions "(new)", which is good. The shutdown says "use four days' leave," which omits that those are the non-public-holiday days, and gives the alternatives of unpaid leave or make-up time. The scope says "permanent staff" and drops part-time/full-time, which is minor. "The only exemption is for 24/7 warehouse staff... exempt from the shutdown only" is correct. "You will receive your team's high-balance list by 31 October" is wrong, because managers receive the list, not staff, and it is addressed to the reader as if they were a manager. That is a "who decided what" or who receives what error. B also opens with filler ("We would like to draw your attention") and is likely over 120 words. Counting roughly: B is about 190 words, which breaks the limit.

A is more accurate, within the word limit (let me estimate A: about 125 words?). Counting A: title ~7, intro ~13, bullet 1 ~35, bullet 2 ~15, bullet 3 ~20, warehouse ~17, action ~12, so about 119. That is borderline but roughly fine. B clearly exceeds the limit.

A is better on accuracy, concision and the length constraint.

Verdict: A
